explanation: Enamel is about 96% mineral, harder than bone. Yet it contains no living cells, so unlike bone it cannot repair itself once it is damaged.

claims.text: Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body.
Bone, cartilage and fingernail are all softer than tooth enamel.
Tooth enamel is about 96% mineral by weight.
Mature tooth enamel contains no living cells and cannot repair itself, unlike bone.

evidence.restatement: Mature enamel has no living cells, so lost enamel never regrows, unlike bone, which remodels. Early lesions can be re-mineralised, which is not regrowth.

issues.note: Cannot repair itself is a little strong, because early enamel lesions re-mineralise from saliva and fluoride. Both the claim and the explanation hold in the sense lost enamel never grows back, so no change is needed.
